newsitem.title: USA: NASD reg chief says munis getting 'close scrutiny'.
newsitem.headline: NASD reg chief says munis getting 'close scrutiny'.

text.p: National Association of Securities Dealers examiners are emphasizing seven areas when inspecting member firms this year, including compliance with MSRB rules, Mary Schapiro, president of NASD Regulation Inc (NASDR), said Thursday.
"NASD is giving close scrutiny to the municipal securities area," Schapiro said in opening remarks at NASD's Spring Securities Conference here.
"Both NASDR and our members are now benefiting from our bringing in to our staff a director of fixed income securities," Schapiro said.
NASDR announced on April 25 that it hired a former U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency official, Malcolm Northam, as the group's first director of municipal industry compliance.
"That's going to play a key role in assisting firms with compliance" with Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board rules, Schapiro said.
"He also is a focal point for our coordination with the Securities and Exchange Commmission and MSRB," Schapiro said.

Schapiro named six other areas getting special emphasis during inspections this year: sales practices involving small cap securities and variable annuities; suitability of sales of "low price" securities; whether supervisors are adequately monitoring "high risk employees" with disciplinary histories; whether firms are adequately training and supervising telemarketers that make cold calls; and whether firms are complying with two-year-old NASD continuing education standards.
